title: The Work Ownership Decision Matrix
subtitle: Give recurring customer work to the person who can make the binding decision.
intro_text: Use this matrix for one recurring task that currently lands with a senior CSM. Separate the customer consequence from the binding decision, identify the person with authority, then choose whether CS should own, prepare, coordinate, or remove the work.
scoring_note: Do not total the rows into an ownership score. Record the decision, the rightful owner, the CSM contribution, and the stop rule.
closing_quote: Customer proximity creates responsibility for context. It does not create authority over every decision.
next_action: Choose one task that recurs at least monthly. Complete the four sections, name the rightful DRI, and change the next occurrence before redesigning the entire role.
interpretation: CS has the authority, capability, and customer obligation to make the decision
Outcome, decision boundary, and review date
Another function decides and CS contributes customer evidence or a recommendation
DRI, input package, and decision date
CS must preserve customer continuity across a time-bounded handoff
Operational owner, update cadence, escalation path, and stop rule
The work is repetitive, automatable, duplicative, or creates no durable improvement
Automation, process change, or activity to stop

sections.title: Work and Customer Consequence
sections.why_it_matters: A task can matter deeply to the customer without belonging to the CSM.
sections.review_prompt: What customer decision or consequence makes this work necessary?
rows: What happens, how often, and what triggers it?
What changes for the customer if it is late, wrong, or absent?
Is the output a decision, execution, evidence package, update, or handoff?
What observable state means this occurrence is complete?

sections.title: Authority and Capability Test
sections.why_it_matters: Accountability without authority turns the CSM into a permanent escalation layer.
sections.review_prompt: Who can make the binding trade-off and control the resources required?
rows: The exact choice that must be made
Budget, backlog, technical access, policy, or people required
Expert judgement or execution skill the work requires
What is CS held responsible for but unable to decide?

sections.title: Ownership Mode Decision
sections.why_it_matters: A useful boundary specifies what CS still contributes instead of merely rejecting the work.
sections.review_prompt: Should CS own, prepare, coordinate, or remove this work?
rows: CS can decide and the work requires customer judgement
Another DRI decides; CS supplies evidence and recommendation
A handoff needs temporary customer continuity
Work is repeated, automatable, duplicated, or non-durable

sections.title: Handoff and Review Record
sections.why_it_matters: Reassignment fails when the new owner, decision date, and customer communication remain implicit.
sections.review_prompt: What changes at the next occurrence, and how will the team know the boundary held?
rows: One person with final authority for the decision or execution
Evidence, recommendation, context, or customer communication
Event after which CS coordination ends
Did the decision move and did the task return to CS?
